Chapter 10: Reclaiming Black Joy and the Practice of Self-Care.
Let’s talk about something powerful—joy. In a world that so often puts a spotlight on Black pain and struggle, choosing joy isn’t just an act of self-love... it’s a radical move. For many, self-care isn’t a luxury—it’s survival. It’s what helps you keep going, even when life feels like it’s pressing down from every angle.
Imagine this: It’s Saturday morning, and sunlight is pouring through the window. You wake up slowly, take a deep breath, and let yourself enjoy the quiet before the day gets busy. There’s music playing—those songs that instantly remind you of home, of family, and the ways you’re loved. Maybe you cook breakfast, call up a friend just to laugh, and later, you curl up with a book that makes you smile.
Now, these moments might seem simple—maybe even ordinary. But honestly? They’re anything but. In a society that expects Black folks to always be strong, to always push through and carry so much, making the choice to rest, to play, and to find pleasure is actually an act of defiance. It’s like saying, “I am so much more than my struggles. I deserve care, happiness, and peace.”
And here’s the thing—self-care looks different for everyone. For some, it’s therapy or meditation, a way to work through the stress and trauma of daily life. For others, it’s about being creative—maybe writing, painting, dancing, or singing. And for many, it’s simply spending time with people who matter, building memories that heal and sustain you.
Over time, these small acts add up. The practice of self-care becomes a way to reclaim your own power, to say, “This is my life, and I get to shape it.” It’s about remembering that dignity isn’t just about getting by—it’s about truly flourishing. The world might be built for whiteness, but Black joy? That’s a force no one can contain.
Most people don’t notice the quiet strength in these moments. They tend to focus on the fight, on the pain, on the obstacles. But for those living it, joy is both a safe haven and a tool for resistance. It’s a way to stand tall against anything meant to diminish or divide you.
